utterances.text: Okay. We will be looking for that in the transcript. In the meantime, you arrived there, according to your testimony, after Mr. Mladic arrived on the scene, isn't it so? You received a message on the Motorola that Mr. Mladic has arrived, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You came there and you saw these people on the field, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What people are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The people of Milici. You saw the people from Milici on the field, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people from Milic were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes or no. You saw the people from Milici on the field when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I never said that I arrived at the stadium when General Mladic came, and that I saw people from my Milici there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking you -- I'm not saying you said so. I'm asking you a question. Did you see these people from Milici on the field when you got there? That's my question. I'm not saying you said so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment ago, answering the Judge's question I said I didn't know how long --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you see the people from Milici when you got to the field, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether the people were Milici were at the stadium at the time. If they were there, I did see them. If they weren't there, then I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then I don't have any further questions for you. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One short follow-up question. Just to be sure, you had seen the Milici people there earlier, before Mr. Mladic arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even earlier, in the morning. As soon as the capturing of prisoners began, as soon as these prisoners were brought to the stadium, these people began coming to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you assist me again, that was approximately at what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's say around noon time. I can't really be precise. I can't tell you exactly when it was that they began gathering there and when they began coming but when the first prisoners were taken prisoner and taken to the stadium, they probably learned -- heard that there were prisoners coming to the stadium and that's when they began to gather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Save the Chamber the probabilities. We will take a break, and we'll first move into closed session in order to allow you to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Vanderpuye, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good afternoon to you. I have I think about 15, 20 minutes of redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could have in e-court 65 ter 4037.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Malinic, just a few minutes ago you were asked some questions by my colleague Mr. Stojanovic about a sweep operation that was co-ordinated by Colonel Keserovic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually, I've given the wrong number. Let me give you the right number, 65 ter 26128. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember being asked some questions about the sweep operation and your unit's participation in it just a few moments ago in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I want to show you is this document, and you can probably see it now on the screen, yes, there it is. 17 July 1995 is the date, Main Staff of Republika Srpska, you can see in the B/C/S at the bottom of the page typed signature of General Mladic, commander, and you'll find that on the third page in the English, together with a copy of the stamp. So if we can just skip back to the first page in the English, I want to just point something out. You can see it in the B/C/S, though, and you can see that this is a document indicated very urgent and directed to, among other units, the military police battalion of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment. You recall receiving this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could just go to item number 3, I'd like to just take a quick look at that, it's on page 2 in the English. Thank you. And just about the second paragraph in that item, it says: "I hereby appoint Lieutenant-Colonel Keserovic the officer for military police in the Main Staff of the VRS security administration as the commander of all the aforementioned forces." You see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the aforementioned forces are listed there at the beginning of item number 3. Does that comport with your recollection of the units that were engaged in the sweep of the territory indicated in this order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my case, I can say that this part of the battalion that was in Nova Kasaba did take part in the sweep operation activities. I cannot guarantee about the other units. I cannot say that that was that. I didn't have any contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The idea behind this order was to sweep the territory in the zone of the Bratunac-Drinjaca-Milici-Besici village with the aim of discovering and destroying lagging Muslim groups, yes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 26128 receives number P1556, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yesterday - I believe it was at transcript page 12616 - you were asked whether or not your unit received any task in relation to Operation Krivaja 95. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And your answer was that your unit did not participate in the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to clarify with you that when you say your unit didn't participate in that operation, you're referring to the military police battalion as opposed to the 65th Protection Regiment or units of -- other units of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment? Is that right or is that wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily I'm thinking of the battalion of the military police, but I also think that the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment did not have any assignments relating to the Krivaja 95 Operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Then let me show you 65 ter 4037. This is a document dated 21 July 1995. It's issued by the Main Staff of the VRS, and if we go to page 3 in the B/C/S and page 3 in the English, I think we'll see that it's signed, I believe, by General Mladic, not for, but in any event, issued by General Mladic. And what I want to draw your attention to is - if we can go back to the first page very quickly- we'll see that it's an order and it refers to Srebrenica in particular. And it says on the basis of the situation observed in Srebrenica municipality, the conclusion has been reached that civilian organs of power are functioning in a disorganised manner. And the intent of the order, if you read it through, basically is to establish normal and living and working conditions in the region, and General Mladic orders that a commission be formed and names a number of personnel, then he, in item number 3, assigns certain tasks to the commission. And what I want to do is I want to take you to item number 3.8 which should be on page 2 in both versions. Item 3.8 refers to the commission president to be Colonel Lazar Acamovic to report directly to General Mladic about the work being carried out. And item 4.1 just below that refers to the MUP and members of the military police units to clear the terrain and mop up remaining fundamentalist groups. Do you recall receiving a task in relation to that assignment or this order? And if you don't, just let us know.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I ever received any assignments in relation to this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you to item number 6, that's on page 3 in both versions. And in this item we see that General Mladic orders that the commission provide the following war booty for the needs of units that participated in combat, and I remind you that this is in reference to Srebrenica as all of the other provisions are. And it names the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment, the 67th Communication Regiment, and the sabotage battalion. So were you aware that these units participated in combat in relation to Srebrenica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the activities of the 13th, 14th and 15th of July as being integral part of the battles for Srebrenica, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're aware, Mr. Malinic, that Srebrenica fell to the VRS on the 11th of July, Tuesday; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So there was no battle for Srebrenica on the 13th, 14th or 15th; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The combat operations towards Srebrenica were initiated by the VRS before the enclave fell on the 11th; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So my question is: Were you aware of the participation of the units mentioned in this item 6 of this order, their participation in the combat in relation to Srebrenica; that's the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment, your unit, the 67th Communications Regiment and the sabotage battalion as indicated here? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment did not take part in the fighting for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you done with the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I have one or two additional questions. Did you receive any of those items there, that is colour TV sets, video recorders, freezers and washing machines for your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military police battalion that was in Nova Kasaba did not receive any of the items that are in this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I meant to ask you whether the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment received any of these items.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not aware if the rest of the regiment received any items from the war booty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just have one more question in relation to this document before I tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Item 5 of this document indicates that all heavy machinery and trucks as well as UNPROFOR equipment shall be - and the translation - considered part of VRS war booty. I ask you this question in relation to the vehicles that were left behind by UNPROFOR members when they went to your battalion command in Nova Kasaba on the 13th of July. Do you recall them having been returned, that is the soldiers having been returned to Potocari at their command without their vehicles which remained at your command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two vehicles remained in Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened to those vehicles? Were they returned to UNPROFOR members, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those vehicles were not returned to UNPROFOR. They were used in the military police battalion, one in the regiment and one in the MP Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 4037 receives number P1557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. I've one additional question. Earlier, when you told us that there were claims that UNPROFOR members had been deprived of their belongings and that you said, Well, we listed all that, we tried to find out, could have been civilians who would have done that or military. You didn't know. And you expressed that it was improper to take such goods from UNPROFOR. Have you any explanation why you considered it to be proper to use their vehicles and not return them to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The vehicles that stayed in the barracks in Nova Kasaba were used when the DutchBat left Potocari and went either towards Belgrade or, actually, once they left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that -- makes it -- what makes the difference if you want to return something which is inappropriately taken from? I mean, you could have offered it to be returned, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That battalion left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so I did not have the possibility of returning it to anyone at any place, whereas the kind of unit that we were required vehicles. There was a shortage. So we used it well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you had no possibility. You could have raised the matter with your command and say, Well, we still have two vehicles which should be returned to the legal owners, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. The command was informed and this was not information that was concealed. Lieutenant Egbers, when he was leaving - that was the lieutenant who was heading the UNPROFOR force in Kasaba - received a receipt, other than the list of equipment, also a receipt that he left those two vehicles in Nova Kasaba. Communications equipment that was in that -- in those vehicles is something that Lieutenant Egbers dismantled and took with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was what did you do to return it to UNPROFOR, if anything at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't do anything, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, you say when Lieutenant Egbers left, he dismantled the communication equipment in the cars. You also said you had no possibility to hand back the cars to that -- to the DutchBat people. When he dismantled the communication equipment, why wasn't he just given the whole car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the problem with their departure from the Kasaba sector to go to Potocari was a problem of a security nature. At any point in time, Lieutenant Egbers could have left the area with his vehicles and his men, but he did not dare to do that due to personal safety concerns on the way from Kasaba to Potocari, because at that time combat actions were being carried out in that area. The information that I have is that he was given permission to leave the vehicles and to transport himself and his men and their personal equipment that they had in APCs to the Potocari base. That was a way to do it with the least amount of risk, both for him and for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. At page 56, lines 20 to 25, you say: "Yes, of course. The command was informed and this was not information that was concealed. Lieutenant Egbers, when he was leaving - that was the lieutenant who was heading the UNPROFOR force in Kasaba - received a receipt, other than the list of equipment, also a receipt that he left those two vehicles in Nova Kasaba." Now, was that when he was -- where was he returning to at that stage? Was he going to Potocari or was he going to Belgrade? Because you said the vehicles were used when they went to Belgrade earlier. When did he receive this receipt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They stayed until the 14th or the 15th of July in Kasaba, and then they went to the Potocari base. I think that at around the 20th of July, the entire DutchBat left the Potocari area, and as far as I can remember, they went to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. And you said earlier that when they went to Belgrade, these vehicles were used, although you didn't tell us by who.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that once they left Potocari, we started to use those vehicles for the needs of the military police battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. Do you -- am I right to say you said these vehicles were used to transport these people to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. That is not correct. I said that those vehicles were used only once the battalion of UNPROFOR left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As far as I know and remember, their destination was Belgrade and then from there they probably returned to the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just wanted to show you, if I could, a 65 ter 4179. It was a document that was put to you during your cross-examination not too long ago. You were asked a number of questions both by Mr. Stojanovic and also by the Chamber concerning this document, and I'm not going to go over those. But you can see this document is directed to the commander of the Main Staff, that would be General Mladic, for his information and the assistant commander for morale, religious and legal affairs of the Main Staff, and just for the record, can you tell us who that is? Or was at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assistant commander for morale, religious and legal affairs was General Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: General Gvero you knew well back from 1977, when he was your teacher; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the principal of the school that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And both he and General Miletic, to your knowledge at the time, were the only senior officers at the command post on 13 July 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were asked by my colleague, Mr. Stojanovic, whether you spoke to General Miletic regarding this document on 13 July 1995, and you said that you probably didn't; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you speak to General Miletic at all on 13 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you speak to him regarding the prisoners that were under your control as is indicated in this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether we discussed the prisoners specifically or something else, I don't know, but probably we did discuss the situation in the area where I was. That we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, you said, "probably you did" and then you said "you did." So which is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I say that I probably discussed this or spoke with General Miletic --- but if I did, then we discussed the situation which would then also include the prisoners that were in the territories in my -- in the territory in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you discussed the prisoners that were in your area of responsibility with General Miletic, what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the details of that conversation. This was 18 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Malinic, I can't say that I'm surprised by that. But do you remember testifying in the Tolimir case at transcript page 15372, and being asked by me, "Did you contact General Miletic?" at line 19, and giving this answer at line 20: "In all likelihood during the 13th I did speak to General Miletic." And it continues: "It seems he was the only general in the Main Staff command post. And the other officers from the Main Staff command starting with the commander as well as the Chief of Staff were outside the area of the command post. They were somewhere in the field." You go on to say: "We probably spoke, if you're trying to ask me whether I discussed this," meaning this very document the Chamber has now in front of them, "or something else, as General -- such as General Miletic inquiring about the situation in Nova Kasaba, then I'd say there is a high probability that we did talk." So with respect to the prisoners, I ask you, what did General Miletic tell you to do with them or about them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that General Miletic did not say anything to do with the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the time that you spoke to him on 13 July, your entire day was consumed with securing these prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was one small part of what we did, one of the activities, but we spent most of the time protecting the front line and supporting the combat operations that were underway on that day. Part of our job was to secure the prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You requested backup units to help you deal with prisoners on the morning of 13 July because you only had 20 people at your disposal; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you used the people that you asked for backup to go and man the lines as opposed to the purpose for which you asked them for, which was to help you secure and deal with the prisoners that were surrendering in the hundreds and up to over a thousand during that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is misleading the witness. I would like Mr. Vanderpuye to point to the witness where it was that he said that he asked for reinforcement in order to secure the prisoners and I believe that he said that his request for assistance was of a completely different nature. In the morning on that day, he didn't have those prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you're invited to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember testifying that you called your Chief of Staff, Jovo Jazic, on the morning of 13 July in relation to the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called the Chief of Staff because of the situation I found myself in, a small number -- an insufficient number of soldiers and the fact that I was unable to stop the breakthrough of the 28th Division along the axis.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear exactly which axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat what axis you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The axis Srebrenica-Tuzla, which is where this group was trying a break through.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also communicated that to your commander, General -- well, then Lieutenant-Colonel Savcic that morning; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I briefed him on the situation that we were in, in order to justify why I was requesting reinforcement in that sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You used those units to secure the prisoners that were held at the school.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry, not the school - I misspoke - at the stadium and at the school which is the command post of your unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the main reason why these units -- or, rather, why I requested reinforcements of this segment that was in Kasaba was in order to prevent the breakthrough of members of the 28th Division along the axis where I was. At that time, I didn't know how many prisoners there would be. At that time, I didn't have any information as to whether there would be 100, 200, 300 or 500 prisoners at the stadium. The main reason why I requested reinforcements was in order to secure the facility where I was. Secondly, to take control of that communication and prevent the breakthrough of members of the 28th Division. That is the main reason why I asked for reinforcements. Now, the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last portion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer? You said, "That is the main reason why I asked for reinforcements," and then you continued by saying, "Now, the --" and what you then said, could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the consequence of the taking of prisoners or their surrender, the surrender of the members of the 28th Division, and the number of prisoners in Nova Kasaba, who were held at the pitch, they were the result of our attempt to stop the breakthrough of members of the 28th Division towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. This document that you have in front of you is entitled, "The procedure for treatment of war prisoners"; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it refers to people that were in your custody, particularly a thousand members of the former 28th Division of the so-called BiH army. That's the language; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it's accurate as to your recollection concerning the number of prisoners you had at around 2.00 in the afternoon as is indicated in this document; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the number of prisoners can best be seen in the aerial photo where they were lined up at the stadium. Whether that was 1.000 or fewer, I've already said last time that this Tribunal has the means and the personnel in order to be able to establish exactly the number of people, but I've said that that number was, in fact, smaller than stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You had several hundred prisoners in your custody and control at around the time that this document is timed and on the date that it was sent; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we do that, I would like to put a question to the witness in relation to this document. In the B/C/S version, on the lower left side, there is some handwriting. Please read what you can see and identify what is written there? No, please, it was on the screen. Please bring it back, the original B/C/S version. I'm only interested in that. Can you please read that part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Delivered at 1510, the 13th of July, 1995," and there is a signature. I cannot figure it out. I believe the first letter is M, but it's in Cyrillic script that I can read, but I can't really read exactly the last name of the person who signed this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the English translation, I see a name Gojkovic with three question marks. It's absolutely uncertain if the translation is correct. I would like to ask you if you know a person with the name Gojkovic who could possibly be the person who made this handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know this person Gojkovic, but in any case, that should be someone from the communications department. But I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to -- just for your information, that individual is RM246 and that might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're giving evidence at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I just want to direct the Chamber's attention to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If that is the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If that is the person, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That makes it evidence, Mr. Vanderpuye --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- rather than just the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do have -- well, I do want to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections, Mr. Stojanovic? Then the number would be, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 4179 receives P1558, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Now, we have seen a document with a related in its content, Mr. Stojanovic. I don't think that you tendered that. Do you intend to do that or does the Prosecution intend to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The number was 65 ter 4026.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President I did intend to tender that document but I wasn't finished yet, unless I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, of course, Mr. Stojanovic used it as well so I wondered whether that will be part of the evidence soon, yes or no. I leave it in your hands, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I was going to go to it next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then we'll wait for that, Mr. Stojanovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have 65 ter 4026 -- wait, I think I have to -- I have to call it up using the document ID number. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think I've got it. I'll have to call up 65 ter 4026 and I understand we have a revised translation uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was not yet there at the end of the previous session but apparently now it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Maybe we can just check it if we go to page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Of the English, yes, thank you, Mr. President. Oh, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is what I saw [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, the document ID is 00917860-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So now we can see the stamp and we can see the received date, et cetera. What I wanted to ask you about was item number 4 and item number 4, as you can see, relates to the entry of local and foreign journalists, essentially being prohibited except for journalists of the Main Staff press centre. Do you know under what sector the Main Staff press centre fell back in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was -- it fell under the morale sector, that department.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The morale sector was headed by General Gvero, one of the generals that you said was at the Main Staff command post on 13 July 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: General Gvero was also indicated on the previous document I showed you, which is P1558, that's the 13 July document that was sent 1510 hours and timed at 1400 hours, concerning the thousand prisoners in your custody. General Gvero's name -- I mean his position, at least, is indicated on that document as a person to receive the information proposed by the assistant commander for security and intelligence; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as far as you're aware, the journalists that you saw at the football stadium on the 13th were accompanied by members of the press centre of the Main Staff of the VRS, which is why you let them in; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so [Realtime transcript read in error "soon"] they would have been authorised by the Main Staff of the VRS under the auspices of General Gvero's sector to be present on the 13th of July, 1995, filming what was going on; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that's the case. They had the authority, and they were the only ones who could approve the filming of something, so I'm referring to the General or rather the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This document that we are looking at here is directed to the command of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment, amongst several other units; right? And that would be your command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 65th regiment, yes, that was my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if I'm not mistaken, your recollection is that you didn't receive this document or the assignments that are indicated in it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can recollect this, not in this format. This is an order issued to the regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So if you were to receive tasks related to this order, they would come through your commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Savcic, at the time, or the deputy or Chief of Staff of the regiment, Colonel Jovo Jazic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you receive orders or instructions from either Lieutenant-Colonel Savcic or Jovo Jazic related to anything that you see in this order from General Mladic, to the best of your recollection? And if you don't remember, just say you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that I have to -- may I -- I would like to apply to replace the translation prior to tendering it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think until it's MFI'd or until it's -- that you're still -- but if the old one is still there, then you would need approval to change it, but let me just consult with Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are two options, Mr. Vanderpuye. Either you do it within a second and then we'll admit what is then the English translation, or otherwise you have it now uploaded as a separate document, we admit it, and then you ask later for it to be replaced, and I think that permission will be granted to do that. So let's perhaps proceed at this moment on the basis of what we find under this number in e-court. Madam Registrar? You have given the number already.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, I haven't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you haven't.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So document 04026 receives reserve number P1559, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1559 is admitted into evidence. We expect soon a request for replacing the English translation. Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just bear with me for one second. I lost my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were asked a series of questions about this list that you say was prepared in relation to the prisoners at the school. Now, in your prior testimony, you did -- you were presented with a photograph, an aerial image, of the football stadium. Do you recall that and having marked that exhibit in court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Chamber, the discussion concerning that is at transcript pages 15349 through 15351 in the witness's prior testimony, which I think is P1555.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to show you one other document, and that's P1280.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Definitely shouldn't be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is another intercept, and it's from 1602 in the afternoon. It's a conversation between X and Y - hopefully we'll have the English up in a minute - 1602 in the afternoon of 13 July and it refers to an "extension down at Kasaba, 394," that's what X says, and Y acknowledges that, and then X says, "Where Malinic's unit is, they said that there is some 1500 gathered at the stadium." And we see the response and he repeats it, "There are some 1500 at the stadium in Kasaba," and so on and so forth. To your recollection, is that accurate at that time of day? That's about a half an hour after the document that was sent by General Savcic or Lieutenant-Colonel Savcic was timed.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct data.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the list that you compiled, you said that you gave it to Jovo Jazic, Colonel, your Chief of Staff, I mean, rather, the Chief of Staff of the regiment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps at around the 20th of July. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So for about a week, you had custody of that list at the battalion command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge of the events concerning these prisoners, did you come into any information as to what happened to them between the time that you compiled that list and the time that you gave the list over to Jovo Jazic on or around the 20th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have precise information about what happened to the prisoners from the Kasaba stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Since you turned the list over to Colonel Jovo Jazic, is it fair to say that you've never seen that list again?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you've never seen any video footage that you say was shot by members of the press acting within the auspices of the press centre of the Main Staff of the VRS on 13 July 1995 at or around the stadium where you were securing at least a thousand prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have the possibility because there was no TV signal in Kasaba, and for a while there was also no electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the footage that you say was shot on that day at that time, to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Malinic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have a few more questions. The first, I asked you what was the distance between Milici and Nova Kasaba and I think you said 2 to 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That still is your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know to the metre but I do stand by what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I invite the parties to agree on the distance between Milici and Nova Kasaba? It should be a matter which is such that it should be resolved without further dispute. When could we hear from the parties? And I am talking about the distance by road from the one place to the other. And for Nova Kasaba, I would prefer to have it done in relation to the football pitch. Then I have one other question for you. I was a bit puzzled by one of your previous answers. Were you asked by Mr. Vanderpuye that. "... as far as you were aware, the journalists you saw at the football stadium..." that "... they were accompanied by members of the press centre of the Main Staff, and that is why you let them in..." You answered: "Yes." The next question was: "Soon they would have been authorised by the Main Staff of the VRS under the auspices of General Gvero's sector to be present on the 13th of July, 1995, filming what was going on; right?" And then you said: "Well, I assume that's the case. They had the authority, and they were the only ones who could approve the filming of something. So I'm referring to the General or, rather, to the Main Staff." I understand that you are saying, Those I saw on that day, journalists filming, were the ones I assume who got permission later on that day. Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. And I didn't say that. What I said was that the order for the filming came to me from Jazic and that those crews were given permission to record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what you said earlier. But I'm now reading and that's exactly what created some confusion, the answers you gave to Mr. Vanderpuye's questions. And I read them literally. The reason why I'm asking questions is because indeed you said something different before. Mr. Vanderpuye, or is -- am I mistaken by --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No you're absolutely correct. The problem is I think I was mistranscribed. Because my question was, "So they would have been authorised" and not "soon," and that's, I think, part of the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But even an authorisation by the higher up levels. So let me then again put to you what the question was, but wrongly transcribed although only in a detail, that they, you saw there, there, and which you said were accompanied by the members of the press centre, that you assumed that those were the ones who were authorised to be there. That's at least -- I could read it again to you in its entirety, if you would prefer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I completely understand. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you assumed that they were there, those who, as you've seen in the document, later received authorisation to be there. That was your assumption, is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that you misunderstood me. They had authorisation to come and film. They already came with this authorisation to come and film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Authorisation by whom?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Authorisation from the Main Staff, and in that situation, from General Gvero, because the press centre was part of the organ that he was head of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. You said they had already permission, that's why they were there. But that permission, as you said they had, was not in line with what we see in the order later that day. Do you have an explanation for that? That they were there, where we see later an order from the same competent authority, which, as a matter of fact does not allow them to be there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unable to comment on the difference in the order from the same organ. I don't know what happened for the order to change so that the filming would not be permitted. They were doing their job, the crews that were there. They were interviewing the prisoners, they were filming that entire area during the time that they were there, completely everything. They were -- those journalists who were working in front of the cameras were conducting interviews with certain prisoners. This is what has stuck in my mind. With whom, who, and how, that's something that I cannot say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And later that day, the order is that only journalists of the Main Staff of the VRS could be allowed in. Do you have any explanation why that changed so much during that day, if it did, because we saw an earlier document which goes in the same direction.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no explanation, Mr. President. I'm not the person able to comment on orders of superiors, so I'm unable to tell you what the reason for that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any possibility that the journalists you saw during the day, doing their job there, that these were exclusively journalists of the Main Staff of the VRS and not any outsiders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN MALINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no possibility of that because I already said that there were different TV crews. It was not just those from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, have our questions triggered any need for further questions or the questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I put on the record that a revised English translation of P1559 has been uploaded in e-court and that therefore you -- I hereby order Madam Registrar to replace the existing P1559 English translation, which was doc ID 0092-0086 with the revised version of the English translation uploaded as doc ID 0091-7860-ET. This then concludes your testimony in this Court. Mr. Malinic, I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties, and I wish you a safe return home again. We will move into closed session in order to allow you to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness 269, before you give evidence in this Court, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please be seated. Witness, some protective measures apply in relation to your testimony. The protective measures being face distortion, voice distortion and pseudonym. No one will hear your own voice outside this courtroom, no one will see your face outside this courtroom, and we'll not address you by your name but we'll address you as Witness RM269. Apart from that, I would like to inform you about the following. I'll read the gist of a rule which is applicable in this Tribunal. If you, as a witness, if you would object to making any statement, that is to answer a question, which might tend to incriminate yourself, then you may address the Chamber. Now, we still could compel you to answer that question, but then those answers could not be used as evidence in subsequent procedures. I just want you to be aware of that right to object if that would be -- if that would apply to any of your answers in relation to the questions put to you. There is one exception. If you would not tell us the truth, then your testimony could be used against you if you were -- would lie, or if you would violate the solemn declaration you have just made a minute ago. Are you -- do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you'll now first be examined, although today only for a very limited time, by Ms. Hochhauser. Ms. Hochhauser, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, Witness, thank you for your patience in waiting to begin your testimony. I know that you do speak some -- speak and understand some English, so I'm going to ask you to always make sure to wait until the B/C/S translation is finished and you've heard the complete question in your own language, okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 28972 under seal on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: When you can -- is there something appearing on the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RM269
utterances.text: No. Now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, please, whether that accurately records your name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: RM269
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this Exhibit 289 -- excuse me. 28972 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28972 receives number P1560 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1560 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Witness, you previously testified before this Tribunal in the Popovic case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM269
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Before coming to testify in this case, did you have the opportunity to listen to the audio recording of your testimony in the Popovic case?

utterances.speaker: RM269
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And were your answers in that case both truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: RM269
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Was there anything upon listening to that audio recording that you wanted to change or correct about your answers?

utterances.speaker: RM269
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today that you were asked then during that trial, would you give in substance the same answers?

utterances.speaker: RM269
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 28971 under seal which is relevant excerpts from that testimony as well as the one associated exhibit which is a photograph, 65 ter 04953.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that there are no objections. Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28971 receives number P1561, and document 04953 receives number P1562, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both are admitted into evidence. Any need to have the first one under seal? Or the second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The second one there is no need, Judge, that's 04953, the first one which is the testimony, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, P1561 is admitted under seal. P1562 is admitted as a public exhibit. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might read a brief public summary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In July of 1995, RM269 was in the VRS. After the fall of Srebrenica, RM269 was at the elementary school in Orahovac. At the school, RM269 saw Jasikovac, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade military police, as well as Drago Nikolic, chief of security for the Zvornik Brigade, along with members of the Zvornik Brigade military police and Zvornik Brigade soldiers. Muslim prisoners arrived at the Orahovac school and were taken into the gymnasium. After several hours, the prisoners were taken from the gymnasium bound and loaded by military police into a truck with their hands tied. The truck drove out of the school yard and turned in the direction of Tuzla, and each time after the truck left, shots could be heard, after which the truck returned empty and would take more prisoners. This continued until the gym was emptied of prisoners. RM269 observed military police officers from the Zvornik Brigade on these -- running -- running in proximity to the truck on these trips and heard them say that the prisoners who had been taken away had been killed. The following day, RM269 was sent to the school in Rocevic. At Rocevic prisoners were already in the school and the witness observed dead bodies of Muslim prisoners dressed in civilian clothing. Eventually the prisoners from Rocevic were boarded on to trucks and the witness later learned that they were executed in Kozluk. That concludes my summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. We have a couple of minutes left for a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could please move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 14th day of June, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
